title: Param validator fuzz harness and error metadata enrichment
creator: Maya Chen
description: Design and implement an enriched JSON parameter validation system and a parallel fuzz-testing harness. The goal is to produce machine-actionable, developer-friendly error metadata for tool/function calls while preserving backward compatibility and minimizing runtime overhead. Deliverables: (1) schema extension for optional error-hint metadata, (2) runtime validator changes that surface structured error fields (error_code, span, severity, suggested_fix, example_fix), (3) a fuzz/coverage harness to exercise edge cases and surface mismatches between schema and runtime, (4) SDK mappings for human-friendly messages, and (5) telemetry codes and sampling rules for noisy errors.
acceptance_criteria: Introduce a schema extension field (x-redwood-error-hints) that authors can optionally include in JSON parameter schemas without breaking legacy validators
Runtime validator returns, for any validation failure, a stable set of top-level string fields: error_code, user_message, machine_hint, field_path, span_start, span_end, severity
Validators preserve current error text for existing callers unless the caller opts-in to structured errors via an Accept header or an SDK flag
Fuzz harness discovers at least 95% of schema-required edge cases in the canonical test corpus and produces reproducible traces for failures
SDKs (JS and Python) expose a convenience mapping that converts structured errors into an IDE-friendly format with suggested_fix examples
End-to-end tests cover error telemetry ingestion and verify sampling thresholds (default: 1% for high-volume errors, 100% for P0 failures), and all telemetry uses stable numeric codes
Performance overhead for validation (median p50) is <5% for typical request payloads with the new metadata enabled, and <1% when disabled
Implementation includes feature-flagged rollout plan and a canary in a single customer org before wide release
technical_notes: Schema extension design: use x-redwood-error-hints at the same level as properties in JSON Schema. Allowed keys: suggested_fix (string), examples (array of strings), severity_hint (string enum: low|medium|high), telemetry_code (string). This stays optional and ignored by older validators.

Runtime validator changes: modularize validation pipeline to return a canonical ValidationFailure record exposed as flat string fields in the API layer. Avoid nested JSON in surface contract to simplify SDK consumers.

Error codes: define stable string codes with short namespace 'RVD.' (e.g., RVD.MISSING_FIELD, RVD.TYPE_MISMATCH, RVD.VALUE_OUT_OF_RANGE, RVD.PATTERN_MISMATCH). Map legacy text messages to codes in a deterministic table.
Telemetry: attach telemetry_code from schema when present, else map to generated RVD.* code. Add sampling metadata and a severity mapping for ingestion pipeline.

Backcompat: maintain existing textual errors unless the client sends Accept: application/vnd.redwood+json;version=2 or toggles SDK structuredErrors flag. This preserves current behavior for all customers by default.

Fuzz harness: implement generative fuzzing that uses field shapes + constraints (minLength/maxLength/enum/format) to produce boundary cases; include corpus replay mode to recreate failing traces with deterministic seeds.
Security: redact sensitive values from suggested_fix and examples before storing or sending to telemetry. Default redact rules: token-like strings, email addresses, and long numeric sequences.
SDK ergonomics: JS SDK returns an ErrorWithMeta containing machine_hint and suggested_fix; Python SDK returns a StructuredValidationError with .to_human() helper.
Exposing spans: span_start/span_end are byte offsets into the raw request body. For streaming inputs we will fallback to field_path only; streaming byte offsets are not required in MVP.
Testing: add unit tests for mapping table, fuzz harness regression tests, and integration tests against a toy tool manifest repository.
implementation_plan: Design review (2d): finalize x-redwood-error-hints spec and mapping table. Deliverable: confluence doc and spec JSON examples.
Runtime prototype (5d): add ValidationFailure canonical record and a feature flag to toggle structured errors at runtime. Do not change default error response yet.
Fuzz harness (6d parallel): implement generator and corpus replay. Integrate into CI with nightly runs and failure artifact storage.
SDK mappings (4d): JS + Python modifications to parse structured errors, expose helpers, and default to legacy text for older endpoints.
Telemetry plumbing (3d): attach telemetry_code and severity to validation spans; add sampling controls to ingestion config.
Canary rollout (3d): enable structured errors for internal test org and one small external customer under NDA. Collect perf/UX/telemetry signals.
Docs & examples (2d): update API docs with schema extension examples, migration notes, and troubleshooting guidance.
Full rollout (1d): flip default flag after signoff and monitor metrics for regressions.
qa_plan: Unit tests for all error_code mappings and behavior toggles
Integration tests simulating legacy clients to ensure they still receive legacy text messages
Fuzz harness nightly runs with regression detection and deterministic replay artifacts stored in S3
Performance benchmark runs comparing baseline vs structured errors at P50/P95/P99 with representative payloads
Manual UX review of SDK error formatting in VSCode and PyCharm with sample developer workflows
Canary verification checklist: validation correctness metrics, error volume deltas, telemetry ingestion health, memory/CPU overhead, and privacy leak scan for example strings
risks: Performance: extra metadata extraction and redaction could increase CPU and latency for large payloads. Mitigation: lazy-evaluate suggested_fix and examples only when structured mode enabled.
Privacy: suggested_fix or examples may inadvertently include PII. Mitigation: built-in redaction rules and a denylist; run privacy audit during canary.
Backcompat: clients may begin depending on new fields before GA. Mitigation: opt-in only via Accept header or SDK flag until stable API version released.
Noise: increased telemetry volume for low-severity errors. Mitigation: default sampling rules and allow project-specific overrides.
SDK fragmentation: different SDKs may format messages inconsistently. Mitigation: shared formatting helpers in a common repo and cross-SDK tests.
